ruler_story: Jaimzha Shatterfin, the Mare-Mother, rules the Stormfang settlements across three north-western islands, Shatter Maw. Captains bring her disputes over crews and passage, but she judges a voyage by the households it must sustain. Her crown rests on the maternal house: senior women carry its memory, settle its obligations and keep its succession visible to every harbor. Jaimzha approaches the Gathering as a ruler with terms of her own, willing to lead the Isles or bargain for protection without surrendering her house's continuity.
dynasty_story: House Shatterfin passes its crown through maternal seniority. Jaimzha's younger sister Skritcha is the initial eligible successor, ahead of Jaimzha's daughters Morzha and Rikkra. Her son Vrosh may serve the realm, but cannot inherit under the Tidemother law. The family's saying is 'The tide returns to its mother.' Its women disagree over how much security a stronger crown can offer, yet share an interest in keeping the house and its obligations intact.
nation_story: Shatterfin's Stormfang people cross the water between Shatterfin, Knifeback and Maw Rock for work, kinship and defense. Crews depend on safe passages and households ashore depend on their return. Jaimzha's authority joins those shores through the maternal house. Cindermaw offers military weight, Brackmaw provisions and Reefhook skilled pilots; each bargain also gives another crown a claim on Stormfang service. Shatterfin seeks a place in the Gathering that recognizes both its maritime contribution and its distinct succession customs.
event_description: Jaimzha Shatterfin, the Mare-Mother, receives the Gathering's summons beside the women of her maternal house. Skritcha asks whose protection will keep both islands secure; Morzha asks what service another crown would demand. Our Stormfang crews cross these waters for kin as well as cargo. Jaimzha will not let their households become an afterthought in another king's muster. Shatterfin may lead the Gathering itself, bargain for an alliance or negotiate an Autonomy or Protection Charter through the Ashen Compact. The Compact changes neither our dynasty nor our current succession law. No pact shall erase the maternal house.
event_answer: The Tidemother brings her own terms.
followup_description: Jaimzha calls her maternal kin to weigh the Gathering's promises. Skritcha, the initial eligible successor, counsels that protection is only useful if the households can meet its obligations. Morzha and Rikkra ask how crews serving a common cause will keep their own shores secure. Vrosh's strength can serve Shatterfin, but military prowess gives him no claim under maternal seniority. The house must choose its friends with the same care it gives its succession. Its saying passes around the table: 'The tide returns to its mother.' These deliberations settle no treaty and appoint no heir; alliances, voluntary submission and leadership remain ours to pursue through the Gathering's existing actions.
followup_answer: Our house shall have a voice among the five.
